opening.text: On a long drive, a good driver stops for a rest. Not because the car is broken. Because the driver needs it. After a short stop, the road looks brighter. God built a rest stop into every week. It's called the Sabbath. He didn't give it to slow us down. He gave it so we can keep going well.

mainMessage.text: The Sabbath is a weekly rest stop given by God. It renews us and draws us closer to Him.

blocks.text: **A gift of rest** God set the seventh day apart. It is a day to rest from daily work and to be renewed.

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
God gave us this special day, not for amusement or daily labor but for a rest from duty, with physical and spiritual relief.
It is a gift of rest.
**The center of the day** The most important stop on the Sabbath is the sacrament. We renew our covenants and remember the Savior.

And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day; For verily this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High;
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
Partaking of the sacrament is the center of our Sabbath day observance.
The sacrament is the center.
**A sign of love** How we keep the day shows how we feel about God. It is a sign between Him and us.

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
What sign will you give to the Lord to show your love for Him?
It shows our love.
**Worship and delight** The Sabbath is more than a day off. It is a day for worship. And Isaiah said to call it a delight.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
The pattern of Sabbath day observance must always include worship.
Worship fills the day.
**Gratitude on Sunday** The Sabbath is a good day to count our blessings. Gratitude opens our hearts to God.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gratitude on the Sabbath Day” from the October 2016 general conference.
We can count all those blessings every Sunday and feel grateful.
Count your blessings.
**Made for us** Jesus Christ taught that the Sabbath was made for people. It serves us, and it leads us to Him.
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
Faith in God engenders a love for the Sabbath; faith in the Sabbath engenders a love for God.
The Sabbath grows our faith.

story.title: God rests on the seventh day

blocks.text: When the creation was finished, God did something we might not expect.

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.
God blessed and made holy the day of rest. We can receive that blessing every week.

opening.text: Your phone does fine all day. But by evening the battery is low. If you don't plug it in, it shuts down. People are the same. After six days of work and worry, we run low. God gave us a day to plug in. It's the Sabbath. We rest, we worship, and we are charged again.

mainMessage.text: The Sabbath is where we recharge. We plug into God and are renewed.

blocks.text: **A day to plug in** God set this day apart for rest and renewal. We don't have to earn it. It's given.

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
God gave us this special day, not for amusement or daily labor but for a rest from duty, with physical and spiritual relief.
It is given, not earned.
**The main charger** The sacrament is where we plug in most fully. We renew our promises and feel His Spirit.

And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day; For verily this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High;
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
Partaking of the sacrament is the center of our Sabbath day observance.
The sacrament renews us.
**A sign we're connected** Keeping the Sabbath is a sign of our bond with God. It shows we want to stay connected.

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
What sign will you give to the Lord to show your love for Him?
It shows we're connected.
**Charge with worship** What charges us is worship. We can sing, pray, read and listen, and call the day a delight.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
The pattern of Sabbath day observance must always include worship.
Worship charges the soul.
**Full of thanks** When we are charged, gratitude comes easily. Counting blessings on Sunday keeps the charge going.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gratitude on the Sabbath Day” from the October 2016 general conference.
We can count all those blessings every Sunday and feel grateful.
Thanks keeps us charged.
**For our good** The Sabbath was made for our good, not as a burden. Jesus Christ is Lord of the day.
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
Faith in God engenders a love for the Sabbath; faith in the Sabbath engenders a love for God.
It is for our good.

story.title: Israel gathers twice as much bread

blocks.text: In the wilderness, the people gathered manna each morning. On the sixth day, something changed.

And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses. And he said unto them, This is that which the Lord hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
They prepared on the sixth day so they could rest on the seventh. A peaceful Sabbath often begins the day before.

application.text: First, pick one task you will finish before Sunday. Second, set aside your phone for part of the Sabbath. Third, spend that time with God or family.

opening.text: Every family has a table. On most days, people eat in a hurry. But on special days, the table is set with care. Everyone sits down together. Nobody checks the clock. Those meals are the ones we remember. The Sabbath is that kind of table. It is set by God, and He invites us to sit down.

mainMessage.text: The Sabbath is a table set by God. We come to rest, to be fed and to be with Him.

blocks.text: **An invitation to rest** God invited us to set the week aside and rest. It's a gift, not a chore.

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
God gave us this special day, not for amusement or daily labor but for a rest from duty, with physical and spiritual relief.
He invites us.
**The bread and water** At the center of God's table is the sacrament. It is where we remember the Savior and renew our promises.

And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day; For verily this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High;
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
Partaking of the sacrament is the center of our Sabbath day observance.
The sacrament is the main course.
**A seat we choose** No one is forced to the table. We choose to come. That choice is a sign of how much we love Him.

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
What sign will you give to the Lord to show your love for Him?
We choose to come.
**Worship together** A table is for sharing. On the Sabbath, we worship together, with family and with our ward family. That brings delight.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
The pattern of Sabbath day observance must always include worship.
We worship together.
**Thanks at the table** Before a good meal, we give thanks. The Sabbath is a day for it.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gratitude on the Sabbath Day” from the October 2016 general conference.
We can count all those blessings every Sunday and feel grateful.
Give thanks.
**The table is for us** Jesus Christ taught that the Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath. It is there to bless us.
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
Faith in God engenders a love for the Sabbath; faith in the Sabbath engenders a love for God.
It is there to bless us.

story.title: Jesus Christ in the synagogue

blocks.text: The Savior was in His hometown, and He did what He always did.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.
Worship on the Sabbath was His custom. It was a habit, not a one-time thing. Habits like this shape a life.

opening.text: A wise farmer lets one field rest. For a season, nothing is planted there. The soil recovers. The next crop comes in stronger. Without rest, even rich soil wears out. God gave us the Sabbath for the same reason. It lets our hearts recover so that we grow well.

mainMessage.text: The Sabbath is rest for the soil of our souls. We recover, and then we grow.

blocks.text: **Rest that renews** God set apart a day for rest from daily work. Both body and spirit are restored.

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
God gave us this special day, not for amusement or daily labor but for a rest from duty, with physical and spiritual relief.
Rest brings renewal.
**What we plant on Sunday** Resting doesn't mean doing nothing. The best thing we plant on the Sabbath is the sacrament and the promises we renew.

And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day; For verily this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High;
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
Partaking of the sacrament is the center of our Sabbath day observance.
The best seed is the sacrament.
**A promise in the soil** When we let the field rest, we show we trust the harvest. Keeping the Sabbath is a sign we trust God.

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
What sign will you give to the Lord to show your love for Him?
It shows our trust.
**The good that grows** Our delight grows when we worship. Isaiah said we would delight ourselves in the Lord.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
The pattern of Sabbath day observance must always include worship.
Delight grows from worship.
**Thankful soil** The best soil is one that holds water. A grateful heart holds the Lord's blessings.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gratitude on the Sabbath Day” from the October 2016 general conference.
We can count all those blessings every Sunday and feel grateful.
Gratitude holds the water.
**A field tended for us** The Sabbath is tended for our good. Jesus Christ is its Lord, and He cares about our growth.
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
Faith in God engenders a love for the Sabbath; faith in the Sabbath engenders a love for God.
He tends the field for us.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they did good on the Sabbath for someone in need. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Christ heals on the Sabbath

blocks.text: Some leaders tried to trap the Savior over a Sabbath rule. A man with a withered hand stood before Him.

And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him. And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
The Sabbath is a day to do good. Serving, visiting and lifting others fit it well.

application.text: First, plan one act of service for next Sunday. Second, visit or call someone who is alone. Third, rest well, knowing you have done good.

opening.text: An old clock keeps good time only if someone winds it. Skip a week, and it slows down. Then it stops. Winding takes just a minute. But it keeps the whole clock running. The Sabbath is our weekly winding. We pause, we turn toward God, and the week ahead runs better.

mainMessage.text: The Sabbath winds our spiritual clock. A little time with God keeps the whole week running well.

blocks.text: **Time to wind** God gave us a day to stop and be renewed. It keeps us from running down.

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
God gave us this special day, not for amusement or daily labor but for a rest from duty, with physical and spiritual relief.
Stop and wind.
**The key that winds** The sacrament is the key. When we take it, we renew our promises and remember Jesus Christ.

And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day; For verily this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High;
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
Partaking of the sacrament is the center of our Sabbath day observance.
The sacrament is the key.
**Time well kept** How we spend this day tells God how we feel about Him. It is a sign between Him and us.

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
What sign will you give to the Lord to show your love for Him?
It shows our love.
**The gears of worship** Worship keeps the gears moving. Prayer, singing, scripture and the sacrament all turn the wheels.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath and the Sacrament” from the April 2011 general conference.
The pattern of Sabbath day observance must always include worship.
Worship turns the wheels.
**Counting the hours well** A good use of time is gratitude. On Sunday, we can count our blessings one by one.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gratitude on the Sabbath Day” from the October 2016 general conference.
We can count all those blessings every Sunday and feel grateful.
Count the hours well.
**The clock is for us** The clock serves people, and the Sabbath serves us. Jesus Christ is its Lord.
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sabbath Is a Delight” from the April 2015 general conference.
Faith in God engenders a love for the Sabbath; faith in the Sabbath engenders a love for God.
It serves us.

story.title: Alma teaches the people to keep the Sabbath

blocks.text: Alma gathered a new church in the wilderness. He gave them a few clear instructions.
And he commanded them that they should observe the sabbath day, and keep it holy, and also every day they should give thanks to the Lord their God.
He paired the Sabbath with daily thanks. The Sabbath winds the clock, and gratitude keeps it ticking all week.

application.text: First, set a regular time each Sunday for a quiet moment with God. Second, give thanks aloud, even briefly. Third, carry one thought from the day into Monday.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

invitations: I invite you to set a regular time each Sunday for a quiet moment with God.
I invite you to give thanks aloud, even briefly.
I invite you to carry one thought from the day into Monday.
blessings: Sunday will bless your whole week.

closingVerse.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
